substitutes: No bollards? Use lamp posts, trees or a row of bins.
title: The Stunt Double
clue: The block is a film set, and the star does their own stunts, all at ankle height.
reveal: Your dog scouts the neighborhood for low, solid things to step on, over or around. The first five they choose become the day's stunts, filmed as one continuous take at a walk. It is parkour, minus the part where anyone lands hard.
objective: Let your dog pick five low stunts on a neighborhood loop, then run them as one slow take and a reverse take.
instructions: Choose a route away from roads, with low, solid, dry things: curbs, a stump, a flat-topped low wall, a bench base, a row of bollards, a log lying flat. Harness, six-foot leash, treats, 20 to 30 minutes, dry weather only.

Location scout: walk the route and let your dog lead. Stand beside any low flat thing and wait. If your dog steps on, around or under it by their own choice, say 'yes', give a treat and walk on. Note five. Never lure up onto anything above knee height or anything that wobbles.
Check each stunt: dry, not metal (manhole covers, grates), no ice, no wet paint, wide enough for four paws and with clear ground on the far side. Drop any that fail.

The stunt rules: four paws on, a two-second pause, then walk off the end or back the way you came. No jumping down, no running along the top. Your leash stays slack the whole time, and your dog can always say no.
Intermission: stop at the greenest patch and let your dog sniff for a full two minutes with water on offer. Dogs that are wound up get a longer break and a shorter take.

Shoot the take: run your five stunts in order at a walk without stopping. You may say 'action'. You may not say 'jump' or 'up'. Level 2: reverse the order. Level 3: add a slow weave between two posts before each stunt.
Wrap party: no more stunts. Walk home on a loose leash with your dog choosing the route at corners where it is safe, and wipe paws if the ground was gritty.
twist: Your dog writes the stunt list: the first five low things they choose to step on become the shoot, filmed in one slow continuous take.
variations: Easier: ground-level only, a curb walk and a weave through lamp posts, with nothing to step on.
No-yard, rainy-day version: build the set at home with a folded yoga mat, a rolled towel to step over and two chairs to weave around.
Small dog: halve every height and keep everything on solid, flat ground.
Harder: add a pause on each stunt while you take three steps away, still on a slack leash.
completion: It counts when your dog has done one voluntary stunt and you have walked home. If your dog skips every stunt and just sniffs, that is the take.
photoIdea: Your dog mid-pause on a stump or low wall, shot from the side at their level, with the block behind them.
memoryPrompt: Which five stunts did your dog choose, and which one did they refuse?
dietNotes: Tiny treats from the daily ration. Check labels for xylitol; ask your vet about diet limits.
safety: Nothing higher than knee height, wet, metal, icy or wobbly; never jump down, never beside a road.
Check the sidewalk with the back of your hand; skip hot or frosty ground. Skip it for dogs with joint problems.
